newsitem.title: INDIA: India parliament's upper house adjourns till 2 p.m.
newsitem.headline: India parliament's upper house adjourns till 2 p.m.

text.p: The upper house of the Indian parliament adjourned until 2.00 p.m (0830 GMT) for a second consecutive day on Thursday, following lawmakers' demands to discuss a corruption scandal and caste tensions in western India.

Najma Heptullah, deputy chairperson of the Rajya Sabya or upper house, adjourned the proceedings amid uprorious scenes from the protesting members who were demanding a discussion on the corruption scandal in the eastern state of Bihar and caste animosities in the western state of Maharashtra.
The house, which was adjourned for the whole day on Wednesday, will reassemble after lunch.
The Congress party has been seeking the dismissal of the regional Hindu Shiv Sena party government in Maharashtra, accusing it of failure in combating insults to Dalits.

Maharashtra has been rocked by tension between lower-caste Hindus, called Dalits, and upper-caste rivals since July 11 when a statue of socialist activist and Dalit leader B.R. Ambedkar was desecrated.
At least 12 people died when police opened fire on rioters in Maharashtra's capital city, Bombay.
Lawmakers of the Hindu nationalist Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) led the protests against the government of Bihar, embroiled in a $280 million corruption scandal.

Bihar's chief minister Laloo Prasad Yadav, who has been indicted in the corruption scandal by federal police, says he will not resign from his post. He says he is innocent in the case, which involves alleged diversion of animal welfare funds.
Prime Minister Inder Kumar Gujral's ruling coalition is badly divided over its continuing association with a breakaway faction set up by Yadav early this month.
Coalition leaders are scheduled to debate the political deadlock on Friday.
